title: NanoTCAD ViDES, ported to Python 3.13, NumPy 2.x and GCC 14
description:
This record covers the port, not the simulator.

NanoTCAD ViDES is a self-consistent NEGF (Non-Equilibrium Green's Function) and Poisson solver for nanoscale device simulation, developed by Prof. Gianluca Fiori and Prof. Giuseppe Iannaccone at the University of Pisa (© 2004–2010, University of Pisa). All of the physics, the numerics and the scientific design are theirs. The original is at vides.nanotcad.com.

The original source targets Python 2.7 and the NumPy 1.x C API, and therefore does not build or run on a current system. This work is a compatibility port that makes it usable again on modern toolchains, and claims authorship of nothing else.

What was changed:

  • Python 2 to Python 3 C API — PyInt_AsLong and PyInt_FromLong replaced by their PyLong equivalents; PyString_AsString replaced via PyUnicode_AsEncodedString and PyBytes_AsString; Py_InitModule replaced by PyModule_Create with a PyModuleDef, under PY_MAJOR_VERSION guards.
  • NumPy 1.x to 2.x C API — PyArray_DOUBLE, PyArray_CDOUBLE and PyArray_INT replaced by their NPY_ equivalents; PyArray_FromDimsAndData replaced by PyArray_SimpleNewFromData through a compatibility shim; the NumPy header path updated from numpy/core/include to numpy/_core/include.
  • GCC 14 — builds under the stricter defaults of a current compiler.

Verified against the original physics: a (10,0) zigzag carbon nanotube returns a bandgap of 0.9795 eV.
